title: Motifs et théorie de Hodge : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
The page is almost blank. It carries a four-line marginal note at top right that serves as a heading or programme: 'Variations du réseau discret en termes d'un pl[?] [?]-dimensionnel, / Notion de transcendance'.

The neighbouring pages set the context. Let X be smooth projective over a field K of characteristic 0, which need not be a number field. Algebraic de Rham cohomology H^*(X) is a K-vector space with its Hodge filtration F^p. For each 'topology' T on K, meaning an archimedean place or embedding sigma_T: K -> C (or R), one gets the following:
- the completion \hat K_T;
- the transcendental Hodge splitting phi_T, from which the page before defines K- (resp. K_r-) rational subspaces H^{p,q}_T(X) of H^*(X);
- through the comparison isomorphism H^*_dR(X) ⊗_K \hat K_T ≅ H^*(X_T^an, Z) ⊗ \hat K_T, a discrete lattice H^*(X_T^an, Z) (mod torsion) sitting inside H^*(X) ⊗ \hat K_T.

The note says to study how this discrete lattice (the Betti Z-structure) varies as T varies. This should be described in terms of some finite- or infinite-dimensional parameter object: probably the space of embeddings of K into C, which is 'large' when K has positive transcendence degree. The next item is the notion of transcendence: the transcendence properties of the periods relating the K-structure (de Rham) and the Z-structure (Betti).

In modern language this is the period map in the embedding variable. Spread X out over a model S of finite type over Q with function field K. Embeddings K -> C then correspond to generic C-points of S. Moving the embedding moves the Betti lattice relative to the de Rham K-structure, and this is governed by the Gauss–Manin connection and the period matrix. The 'notion de transcendance' points to the transcendence degree of the field of periods, i.e. Grothendieck's period conjecture.

The next page lists the matching problems: 'viscéral' comparison of Betti for different topologies, real structures and splittings for different topologies, and the l-adic and p-adic analogues. So this page is a heading for that circle of questions, not a worked argument.

ideas.what: Dependence of the Betti integral lattice inside de Rham cohomology on the choice of complex embedding/topology of the ground field; variation as the embedding moves

Both ideas are well known and attributed to Grothendieck (the period conjecture) or are standard (period maps). Nothing developed here would be new to specialists.
